reviews.reading_evidence: Read the full five-stanza shore/mind comparison: apparently calm mind; visitor with tea/pakoras, photographer, weekend painter and poet of reflected night lights; their shared assumption; repeated inner wave-strikes; then conditional dipping in nirvanic nectar and fearless confrontation to avoid erosion. Checked every may and the surface/interior distinction and final condition.
reviews.reason: Join the night lights to their reflections with the required possessive relation; the detached original phrase obscured what the poet writes about.
open_questions: Nirvanic nectar in a sacred bottle remains the source metaphor; no identification as alcohol, ritual substance or prescribed practice.
reviews.tradeoff: Preserve the long observational line and following reflected movement; all stanza sizes unchanged.

reviews.reading_evidence: Read the full five-stanza shore/mind comparison: apparently calm mind; visitor with tea/pakoras, photographer, weekend painter and poet of reflected night lights; their shared assumption; repeated inner wave-strikes; then conditional dipping in nirvanic nectar and fearless confrontation to avoid erosion. Checked every may and the surface/interior distinction and final condition.
reviews.reason: Restore the source’s may/try possibilities for photographer, painter and poet; the draft had converted these hypothetical observers into definite future actions.
open_questions: Nirvanic nectar remains a metaphor without an asserted physical or religious referent.
reviews.tradeoff: Repeated सकता carries the actual tentative scenario; it is not varied away merely for elegance. The onlooker already had सकता and remains unchanged.

reviews.reading_evidence: Read all fourteen lines: unexceptional silence at thunder/lull’s threshold, goodbye/forgetting pause and undrunk coffee, folded sari with jasmine/camphor, turmeric dreams and Ganga footprints, falling leaf, smile in time’s cracked lip and continuing presence long after forgotten names. Checked the sensory anchors and the final temporal clause as one continuous sentence.
reviews.reason: Distinguish silence folded in sari creases from being broken; place names inside the Odia forgetting clause rather than after its completed temporal phrase.
reviews.tradeoff: The ending now lands on persistence in time instead of the isolated names; this trades source word placement for a grammatical target clause, preserving all fourteen lines.

reviews.reading_evidence: Read all fourteen lines: unexceptional silence at thunder/lull’s threshold, goodbye/forgetting pause and undrunk coffee, folded sari with jasmine/camphor, turmeric dreams and Ganga footprints, falling leaf, smile in time’s cracked lip and continuing presence long after forgotten names. Checked the sensory anchors and the final temporal clause as one continuous sentence.
reviews.reason: Repair the stranded object of forgetting in the final temporal phrase; silence still remains long after the world forgets our names.
reviews.tradeoff: Names moves into the clause and the last line emphasizes long after. No loss of an image, line or the source’s temporal distance.

reviews.reading_evidence: Read the full four stanzas: Fear as gatekeeper excluding Hope/disaster’s harbinger, deserted still dark castle with birds silent and owls/bats, darkness’s private glory and painful light, torchlit foolish dancing then exhaustion and falls as light fades, and the wasting people as if never there. Preserved the reversal of comforting hope/light and the bleak ending.
reviews.reason: Make too tired to dance explicitly inability, not tired followed by an unattached to dance; clarify darkness as the cause of their faltering.
open_questions: Vision of the dark is left as the source’s unusual personification rather than resolved into a specific philosophy or ideology.
reviews.tradeoff: Keep the break before dance and the causal sequence; do not soften the despair or supply a hopeful resolution.

Source He personifies Hope as male; Hindi आशा is grammatically feminine while अग्रदूत retains masculine form. No added character identity or automatic noun substitution.
reviews.tradeoff: Keep the personified abstract nouns and the source’s unusual vision/taste image rather than explaining it.

reviews.reading_evidence: Read all nine stanzas: grandiose compassionless manipulators and repeated directional bending; painter’s supposed disorder as their sneering question; condescending poses and art criticism while kicking a skeletal dog; painter ignoring them, resumed dabbing/singing and resentful retreat; dog nestling and painter patting it while adding colour; final celebration question. Checked who judges, harms, ignores and comforts; preserved left/right repetition and the human/animal contrast.
reviews.reason: Make the din cause disgust rather than contain disgust, and distinguish mongrel/mixed breed from a specifically native dog.
reviews.tradeoff: The descriptive mixed-breed phrase is longer than mongrel; it preserves the animal without inventing local breed or making the narrator insult it.

reviews.reading_evidence: Read the complete ten-line dawn scene: ripple folding morning, flat palm shadows, village held inside breath, yawning dog, fluttering sari catching sun, ferry-rope/old-sentence creak, wind touching mud walls and staying, two herons trading places, river lowering its voice lest land still sleep. Kept each small action and the restrained auditory close.
reviews.reason: Restore the reciprocal trading of places; merely changing place does not establish the exchange between the two birds.
reviews.tradeoff: No species refinement or added movement; preserve the quiet ten-line sequence and all other images.
